title: validator('form') hands its callback {} for a valid multipart form whose Content-Type has a parameter after boundary, such as multipart/form-data; boundary=X; charset=utf-8, while parseBody() reads the fields

reproduced.base: validator('form') hands {} and the route answers 200 {} for multipart/form-data; boundary=X; charset=utf-8, while parseBody() returns {"foo":"bar"}, on Node 24.22.2, Bun 1.4.4 and Deno 2.9.8 (round 2 probe).
reproduced.head: The same at the head. fix-M4b (ruling 14's patch) and fix-M4a+M4b (ruling 13 and 14's combined patch) each make the validator hand {"foo":"bar"} for the after-boundary header on all three runtimes; the combined patch also cures the space before ';' and the parameter before boundary.

not_run: How often clients send a parameter after boundary was not measured.

maintainer_acknowledgement.quote: A request with another legal parameter, such as `charset`, or with extra whitespace after the `;` is not recognized as a form.

shipped: v4.12.28 (the change); fixed upstream by d88fab37 on 2026-11-01
strongest_argument_against: GT-p4's wording, and ruling 14 that widened it, name a parameter before boundary only. A reader who holds the key to its words would keep the after case apart until the owner widens it, which is what the first grader did.

promise.source: To validate form data, specify `form` as the first argument and a callback as the second argument. (Hono's validation guide; the promise GT-p4 rests on.) MIME recipients ignore unknown parameter names (RFC 2045 section 5.1).

owner-docs.unread: The MIME and FormData algorithm and the cited RFC sections were read; unrelated header-parameter hits were not read closely (ruling 14's note).
owner-docs.found: RFC 9110 section 5.6.6: parameters = *( OWS ";" OWS [ parameter ] ), any number in any order; RFC 2045 section 5.1: MIME readers ignore parameter names they do not know.
